parties:
Mirpur Mazar Co-Operative Market Society Ltd ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Capital Tower (Pvt) Ltd & Ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 8. It has been submitted on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner that in paragraph 3 of the leased deed it has been specifically stated that the plot so allotted to the defendant No. 6-appellant is to be used for commercial purpose and the DW 2, deposing for the defendant No. 6, has stated that it has a plan to construct a building for running a hospital with the expectation of earning profit but in the schedule to the leased deed the plot so allotted to the defendant No. 6 has been described as institutional plot which is in contradiction to the purpose for which land so allotted is to be used as stated in paragraph 3 of the lease deed and, as such, the allotment so made to the defendant No. 6 was not transparent and the said defendant was unjustly favoured and consequently, the allotment so made and the lease deed registered pursuant thereto is tainted with unfairness and the authority in making the allotment violated the provisions of Articles 27 and 144 of the Constitution. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the land in question was allotted at a too low price to the defendant No. 6 upon ignoring the offer of the plaintiff to purchase the same at a fair market price for maintaining its original purpose, that there was no basis for treating the plot allotment whereof was sought for the construction of the hospital that would be run on commercial basis as anything other than a commercial plot and there was no evidence on record that the project was non-profit making or charitable to justify the plot allotted of being described as any other kind of plot than a commercial plot or to justify allotting the plot at an abnormally low price by resorting to the device of naming it as 'institutional' plot so as to confer an undue advantage and unjustly enriching a favoured party, that the lands situate in the locality have been allotted to the others at a price much higher than the price at which land in question has been allotted to the defendant No. 6 and there was no material on record in support of the contrary position that land similar to the land in question at similar location in Mirpur or anywhere near and during the material period was sold at a price as low as the price at which the land was sold to the defendant No. 6, that as in the written statement of the defendant Nos. 1- 5 it was stated that leaving certain portion of land for car park the Master Plan of the area was modified and, as such, evidence of DW 1, that there was only modification of the layout plan of the area ought not to have been taken into consideration, that while the Chief Engineer in his letter dated 29-7-1981 rejected the prayer of the plaintiff for leasing out the land in suit to them for using as the car park mentioning that the land has been marked in the Master Plan as car park and, as such, the DW 1, who deposed for the defendant Nos. 1-5, was not competent to depose that there was a layout plan in respect of the suit land prepared in 1967, that the modification of the plan, as deposed by the DW 1, being for the benefit of the favoured party is an abuse of the authority under Article 144 of the Constitution and violative of Article 27, as well as being an arbitrary act to confer undue advantage to unjustifiably enrich a favoured party is contrary to the public interest, that no material was placed on record to show that 'institutional' plot/plots was sold at such a low price as the plot in question was sold and there was no yardstick for carving out 'institutional' plot out of the plots which are commercial plots and by no yardstick the plot so allotted to the defendant No. 6 can be said to be 'institutional' plot.
